cards.explanation: The answer is that her righteousness shines like a bright light. That's the finish line verse 1 sets: “…until her righteousness shines like a bright light, her salvation like a blazing torch.” Until then, the speaker won't keep still. That is a LOT of not keeping still, friends. My mustache gives out after one batch of cookies.

The answer is the LORD. Verse 2 says it plainly: “…a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow.” The name comes straight from Him. I know a little about getting a name from somebody else, friends. The Millers, the family who bought me for a quarter, carved Dorin on my handle, and I've worn it proudly ever since.

The answer is True. Verse 3 says it: “You will be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of your God.” Notice where the crown is. It's held, not set down somewhere. Most of us can't even hold onto our car keys, and here's a crown being carefully held.

The answer is False. Verse 4 says, “No longer will you be called Forsaken…” Her land won't be named Desolate anymore either. Those two names get retired, friends. Hephzibah and Beulah are stepping in.

The answer is that the LORD will take delight in her. Right after the new names, verse 4 gives the reason: “for the LORD will take delight in you…” So the name comes with a reason attached. That's more than I can say for most names, friends. Mine came with a price sticker.

The answer is that He will rejoice over her. Verse 5 says, “…as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.” Think of a groom at the front of the room who cannot stop grinning. That's the picture, friends. Rejoicing is the word the text uses.
The answer is False. Verse 6 says of the watchmen, “they will never be silent day or night.” Day or night, no quiet time, friends. That's a job with no break room.

The answer is that He makes Jerusalem the praise of the earth. Verse 7 gives the stopping point: “…until He establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.” Until then, they keep calling on Him. So it's a long, steady knock on the door, friends. And the text tells us just where it ends.

The answer is True. In verse 8 the LORD says, “Never again will I give your grain to your enemies for food…” He swears it by His right hand and His mighty arm. That's a promise with a lot of weight behind it, friends. The grain stays with the ones who worked for it.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says it: “For those who harvest grain will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather grapes will drink the wine in My holy courts.” The ones who did the work get the meal, friends. And they praise the LORD. I'd call that a good setup.

The answer is people. Verse 10 says, “Go out, go out through the gates; prepare the way for the people!” So it's road work with a purpose, friends. Think orange cones and a very long to-do list. The road is for the people.

The answer is the nations. Verse 10 ends with the call to “raise a banner for the nations!” A banner is made to be seen, so I think the nations are meant to look at it, friends. Nations came up in verse 2 too, where they see Zion's righteousness.

The answer is to the ends of the earth. Verse 11 says, “Behold, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth…” That's as far as the earth goes, friends. It's a message with a very long delivery route. And it's a message for Daughter Zion.

The answer is Savior. Verse 11 says, “See, your Savior comes!” That's the news carried to the ends of the earth, friends. I think it's the kind of news that makes you drop everything and look. And the very next line has more.
The answer is Sought Out. Verse 12 says, “…you will be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken.” Sought Out is the opposite of left behind, friends. Forsaken had a good run, but the name changes.
